chunks: And Sad ibn Tarif narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said:

A girl was brought before Umar ibn al-Khattab, and witnesses testified against her that she had committed adultery. Her story was that she was an orphan raised in the house of a man who had a wife. The man would frequently be away from home. The orphan grew up to be beautiful, and the man's wife feared that her husband might marry the orphan upon his return. So, the wife called some women from her wife called some women from her neighbors, restrained her, and then violated her with her finger. When her husband returned, he asked his wife about the orphan, and she accused her of indecency and brought forth witnesses from her neighbors to support her claim.

He said: That matter was presented to Umar ibn al-Khattab, but he did not know how to judge it. He said to the man, 'Go with her to Ali ibn Abi Talib.' They came to Ali and told him the story. He said to the man's wife, 'Do you have witnesses?' She said, 'Yes, these are my neighbors who testify against her for what I say.'

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) drew his sword from its sheath and placed it in front of him. Then he ordered each of the witnesses to be taken into a room. Then he called the man's wife and interrogated her from every angle, but she refused to deviate from her statement, so he sent her back to the room she was in.

Then he called one of the witnesses, knelt on his knee, and said to her, 'Do you know me? I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this is my sword. The man's wife has said what she said and returned to the truth, and I have granted her safety. Now speak the truth, or I will fill my sword with your blood.'

The woman turned to Ali and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, safety in exchange for the truth.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said to her, 'Speak the truth.' She said, 'No, by Allah, the orphan did not commit adultery. But the man's wife, when she saw her beauty, charm, and appearance, feared the ruin of her husband. So she gave her intoxicants to drink, called us, and we restrained her, and she violated her with her finger.'
Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest! I am the first to separate the witnesses, except for Daniel.'

Then Imam Ali sentenced the woman to the punishment for false accusation (hadd al-qadhf), and obligated her and those who assisted her in violating the orphan girl to pay her a dowry of four hundred dirhams. He separated the woman from her husband and married the orphan to him, paying her dowry from his wealth.
Umar ibn al-Khattab said, 'Tell us, O Abu al-Hasan, about the story of Prophet Daniel (peace be upon him).'
He said, 'Daniel was a young orphan who had neither father nor mother. An elderly woman from the Children of Israel took him in and raised him.'

And a king among the kings of the Children of Israel had two judges. He had a friend who was a righteous man, and he had a beautiful wife. This man used to visit the king and speak with him. The king needed a man to send on one of his affairs, so he said to the two judges, 'Choose for me a man whom I can send on one of my affairs.' They said, 'Send so-and-so,' so the king sent him.

The man said to the two judges, 'I entrust my wife to your care and advise you to treat her well.' They said, 'Yes.' The man left, and the two judges began visiting the house of the pious man and fell in love with his wife. They tried to seduce her, but she refused. They said to her, 'If you do not yield to us, we will testify against you before the king for adultery, so that they may stone you.' She said, 'Do as you wish.' So they came to the king and testified against her that she had committed adultery. She was well-known for her good and beautiful reputation.

A great matter entered the king's heart; his grief intensified, and he was admiring her. He said to them, 'Your word is accepted, so delay her for three days, then stone her.' He announced in his city, 'Attend the execution of so-and-so, the devout woman, for she has committed adultery, and the two judges have testified against her for that.'
The people began talking extensively about that. The king said to his minister, 'Do you have any solution for this?' He said, 'No, by Allah, I have nothing for this.'

When it was the third day, the minister rode out, as it was the last day for her. He saw naked boys playing, and among them was Daniel. Daniel said, 'O group of boys, come here so that I may be the king, and you, so-and-so, be so-and-so the devout woman, and so-and-so and so-and-so be the two judges who testified against her.'

Then he gathered dirt and made a sword from reeds. Then he said to the boys, 'Take this one by the hand and place him in such-and-such a place,' while the minister was standing and watching. 'And take this one and place him in such-and-such a place.'
Then he called one of them and said, 'Speak the truth, for if you do not speak the truth, I will kill you.' He said, 'Yes,' while the minister was listening.

He said to him, 'What do you testify against this woman?' He said, 'I testify that she committed adultery.' He said, 'On what day?' He said, 'On such-and-such a day.' He said, 'At what time?' He said, 'At such-and-such a time.' He said, 'In what place?' He said, 'In such-and-such a place.' He said, 'With whom?' He said, 'With so-and-so, the son of so-and-so.'
He said, 'Return this one to his place and bring the other one.' They returned him and brought the other one. He asked him about that, and he contradicted his companion in his statement.

Daniel said, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest! They testified against her falsely.' Then he called out to the boys, 'The two judges have testified falsely against so-and-so. Come and witness their execution.'

The minister went to the king promptly and informed him of the news. The king sent for the two judges and brought them in. Then he separated them and did to them as Daniel had done to the boys. They contradicted each other just as the boys had. He then announced to the people and ordered their execution.

key_terms.اقْتَضَتْهَا بِإِصْبَعِهَا: Violated her with her finger (to simulate sexual intercourse)
key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: The punishment for false accuser (hadd al-qadhf)
key_terms.فَرَّقَ بَيْنَ الشُّهُودِ: Separated the witnesses (to question them individually)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (as) use the method of separating witnesses to prove the innocence of the orphan girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights the jurisprudential principle of *al-farq bayn al-shuhud* (separating witnesses), where Imam Ali (as) isolates witnesses to detect collusion, a method he attributes to Prophet Daniel (as). The narrative illustrates the practical application of this technique in exposing a false accusation (*qadhf*) by an orphan's guardian, who had physically manipulated the girl to fabricate evidence of adultery. This event underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on scrutinizing witness credibility and the prophetic precedent for using psychological pressure to reveal truth in legal disputes.
